# Synthetic acceptance controls for the editorial pattern classes.
# Non-comment, nonblank lines must pass all patterns, except the proof examples
# tested through check-body-lint.sh's prose-style exemption. A line starting
# with "# " is a comment; Markdown heading cases use "##" or deeper and are
# asserted like any other line.

# Runtime behaviour and present-tense review vocabulary.
The linter reports an invalid field name
The parser found an invalid record and returned an error
A reviewer opens the configuration page
The audit log records each accepted update
The test suite checks the retry limit
Reviewers can inspect the generated patch
The health check reports a stale cache entry
Static analysis reports unused imports
A review panel displays the current revision

# Ordinary documentation headings.
## Summary
## What changed
## Notes
## Testing
## Proof
### Behaviour

# Runtime actions and initial states.
Callers can configure the timeout
The handler drafted a response before closing the socket
Users initially see an empty list

# Product counts rather than review tallies.
7 of 8 parser paths are covered
The worker retries 3 times
Exit codes: 0 clean, 1 violation, 2 gate error
The queue holds four records
Two workers process the queue
3 of 5 tasks finished before the deadline

# Data capabilities without observed usage claims.
The preferences panel has a reset button
The cache stores playback metadata
The legacy endpoint logs each request
The service serves a static manifest
Telemetry is disabled by default
Sample data is loaded from a fixture

# Wording outside the product-judgement pattern.
Nobody can read a deleted record
The default profile uses a neutral theme

# Technical uses of tool names and local-state vocabulary.
Claude is absent from the runtime path
The codex directory contains example inputs
Conductor tracks are listed in the manifest
Conductor workspace support includes a launch command
Generated files are stored under build/
The cache stash is cleared on shutdown
Files untracked by the manifest are ignored
Pushed builds use the release identifier

# Near-misses: each line sits just outside one gap bound or word anchor, so
# widening that bound or dropping that anchor makes the line match.
The audit log keeps one entry for every accepted configuration update the parser found valid
Caught exceptions from the network client are retried in the audit job
The parser found an invalid record in the nightly configuration audit
Errors found in reviewed files are listed by path
The app's own settings page lists every field, and the export writes the data
Telemetry data stays in the local cache until the user has confirmed the upload
The lint report lists rule7 findings in a separate column
The summary table labels its last column # Findings

# Proof-block punctuation is accepted by the body linter.
- [ ] runtime: n/a — no runtime change
- [ ] build: n/a — documentation only
- [x] tests: proof/tests.log
